title: Investigate GPU pool starvation: queue buildup, KV-cache cold starts, and mitigations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 02:17 UTC a hosted API GPU pool experienced progressive queue buildup and eventual request rejections for ~75 minutes. Symptoms: queue depth grew in affected pools, large tail latencies for streaming generation, autoscaler did not add enough nodes fast enough, and multiple customers saw 503/429 errors. Immediate emergency mitigations included a temporary capacity bump, per-org emergency QPS caps, and rolling back a staging autoscaler change. This ticket collects the root cause analysis, short/medium/long term fixes, owners, and validation plan so we avoid repeat GPU starvation events.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:17 UTC: first sustained queue growth in us-east-1-hosted-pool-3
2026-03-09 02:25 UTC: alert fired (queue_depth > 70% capacity) — oncall acknowledged
2026-03-09 02:35 UTC: throttling and global rate limits applied to reduce inflow
2026-03-09 02:42 UTC: temporary +12 GPUs provisioned from spare reserved pool
2026-03-09 03:10 UTC: rollback of autoscaler tuning patch (was reducing aggressiveness)
2026-03-09 03:50 UTC: queue returned to normal and incident declared mitigated at 03:58 UTC
root_cause: Compound factors: (1) recent change to default batching window increased average per-request GPU occupancy for long-generation jobs leading to slower throughput, (2) a CPU-side regression in request routing deferred prefix/KV-cache warmup causing many cold KV-cache hits, and (3) an autoscaler change deployed the previous day which raised scale-in cooldown and lowered scale-out aggressiveness for a subset of pools.
A single large customer's automated rerun of long stream jobs magnified the effect by concentrating long-lived sessions on a small set of pools.
Monitoring gaps: we lacked an early queue-imbalance alert tied to per-pool KV-cache hit-rate and per-request GPU-occupancy which would have signaled the pattern earlier.
short_term_actions: (Done) Emergency +12 GPU provision from reserved capacity for us-east-1-hosted-pool-3 (owner: infra-oncall).
(Done) Applied temporary per-org QPS caps for high-volume customers that matched historical 99p usage (owner: rate-limiting).
Adjust autoscaler defaults for all hosted pools: reduce scale-out cooldown to 30s and remove the overly-conservative backlog multiplier (owner: infra/autoscale).
Deploy a hotfix to ensure routing warms KV-cache for streaming start requests (owner: serving/runtime).
Add a short-lived queue-depth dashboard and alert that includes KV-cache hit rate as a correlated signal (owner: observability).
medium_term_actions: Implement progressive request shaping: early reject or pause for oversized token requests above model-specific thresholds with configurable per-org policies (owner: api-team).
Build 'warm' standby workers per hot-model: pre-loaded KV cache and model weights on a fraction of nodes to drain cold-cache spikes faster (owner: serving/runtime).
Enhance autoscaler to use per-pool request-duration distribution (p50/p95/p99) instead of only queue length; include fast-burst short-lived nodes in the pool types (owner: infra/autoscale).
Run a load test scenario simulating 10x long-stream bursts for 3 customers to validate new shaping + warm pools (owner: sres)
long_term_actions: Predictive capacity hints: feed historical usage + calendar signals into an ML model to pre-scale pools for known high-demand windows (owner: capacity-forecasting).
Introduce SLA-aware admission policy that reserves headroom for customers with reserved capacity and gracefully degrades lower-tier traffic (owner: product/infra).
Invest in kernel and sequence-aware batching that prioritizes finishing short requests to keep throughput high under mixed workloads (owner: serving/optimizer).
Formalize capacity playbooks and runbook automations for automatic emergency capacity grafting from other regions (owner: incident-response).
runbook_updates: Add a 'GPU pool queue growth' section describing diagnosis steps (check queue depth, KV-cache hit-rate, per-request GPU-occupancy, recent deploys).
Document immediate mitigations and safe rollback steps for autoscaler changes.
Add exact Grafana queries and thresholds to the runbook for 3 alert tiers (warning 50%, action 70%, critical 90%).
testing_and_rollout_plan: Feature branches for serving and autoscaler changes; end-to-end tests in staging with synthetic cold-cache and warm-cache scenarios.
Canary rollout of KV-cache warmup on 1 region and 1 customer cohort (1% traffic) for 72 hours; metrics to monitor: queue depth, tail latency, KV-cache hit-rate, GPU occupancy, and error rate.
If tail latency or error rate increases by >10% vs baseline during canary, abort and revert changes. Otherwise progressively increase to 25% then 100% over two weeks.
Run scheduled chaos test once per quarter that simulates concentrated long-lived sessions on single pool to validate warm pools and admission controls.
acceptance_criteria: New alerts fire at the defined thresholds and are routed to oncall with runbook links.
Autoscaler updates consistently return queue depth to <= 50% within target time during synthetic bursts in staging.
KV-cache warmup reduces cache-miss tail latencies by at least 30% in canary traffic for affected models.
Progressive shaping correctly rejects >95% of known oversize requests before they hit GPU (avoids long-living sessions when overloaded).
monitoring_changes: Add per-pool 'in-flight token count' metric and alert when > 60% of max tokens capacity for >30s.
Emit 'kv_cache_warm' flag per request to enable heatmap of warm vs cold requests per model/pool.
Correlation dashboard: queue_depth vs kv_cache_hit_rate vs avg_request_gpu_time (owner: observability).
notes_and_discussion: 2026-03-10: Postmortem review held with Eng, SRE, Product and Design. Agreed to prioritize warm pools and auto-scaler tuning as top two mitigations (Aisha P, Miguel R).
Design feedback: console should surface per-customer 'burst risk' indicator so sales and CS can proactively contact heavy customers (owner: design).
Product note: consider offering a paid option for 'guaranteed warm pool' for enterprise customers that need consistent tail latency.
